subject: Private VPC: edge validation, control-plane segregation, and governance checklist
messages:
From: Anya Petrov <anya@retailco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: RetailCo Network Team <network@retailco.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC validation request — edge provisioning and control/data segregation

Jordan —

Thanks for yesterday's demo. Before we sign the MOP, our network team needs a short architecture validation: specifically we want confirmation on the control-plane/data-plane segregation at the edge, egress controls for caching nodes, and the expected BGP/SR config on the hop from our colo to the tenant gateway.

Can you share an annotated diagram and a checklist we can use for our audit team? Preferably something we can attach to the SOC evidence bundle.

Also: will the control plane talk directly to our KMS for keywrap, or should we expect a proxy? That’s a gating question for our security sign-off.

Thanks,
Anya Petrov
IT Lead, RetailCo Solutions
[attachment: current-deployments.csv (csv)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@retailco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC validation request — edge provisioning and control/data segregation

Hi Anya —

Appreciate the clear list. I attached a first-pass reference packet that addresses the three items you called out: control/data boundaries, egress design for cache nodes, and the handoff for BGP. High-level answers below; full details are in the PDF (rvc-private-vpc-ref-diagrams-v1.pdf).

- Control plane keys: by default the Redwood private control plane will perform API calls to your KMS via an authenticated proxy in your tenant VPC (we recommend customer-managed proxy for auditability). We can also support direct KMS integration if you provide a cross-account IAM role — we documented both options in section 2.2.
- Control/data segregation: control-plane (management traffic, metrics, config) uses a dedicated VLAN and mTLS-authenticated channels to the control endpoint. Data-plane inference traffic never traverses that VLAN and terminates on the tenant gateway. Diagrams show the path and logical ACLs.
- BGP / hop: we expect a single BGP peering from your colo leaf to the tenant gateway with /30 service IP assignment. We included the sample BGP policy and community tags.

Next steps:
1) Can your network team review pages 4–7 of the PDF and flag any non-starters?
2) If that looks good, Kimberly will run the MOP acceptance checklist and circulate the signed copy.

Call availability: I can do a 30-min sync tomorrow 10–11 PST if helpful.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[attachment: rvc-private-vpc-ref-diagrams-v1.pdf (pdf)]

  * Confirm that the tenant gateway supports BGP MD5 — RetailCo prefers MD5 for peering auth; if not, we need to propose an alternative.
  * Fill in explicit CIDR allocation appendix (page 7) with the /30s and reserved ranges (Lauren).

Kimberly

Kim / Jordan — quick notes from infra on the KMS and peering: 

- KMS: customer-managed proxy is supported and preferred for security teams since the proxy provides an auditable TLS termination point and can be instrumented with SIEM. For direct KMS roles we recommend short-lived credentials via STS and a narrow-scoped role; both approaches are documented.
- BGP MD5: our tenant gateway firmware supports MD5 and BFD on the peering. We'll include the exact sample config in the appendix (showing local-as, remote-as, password, timers).

I'll update the PDF appendix and push v1.1 by COB today.

—Aditya
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks for the packet. A few clarifications from our side after internal review: 

- We want the MOP to include an evidence step that proves control-plane cert rotation took place and was logged to our SIEM (we can provide a collector).
- Can you confirm the expected TLS cipher suite list for the mTLS channels? We need to add this to our procurement acceptance.
- One more ask: include a short paragraph that describes failure modes (control-plane loss, gateway failover, and cache-stale scenarios) and recommended mitigations.

If you can add those items to v1.1 we'll do a final pass and aim to sign next week.

—RetailCo Network Team

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private VPC validation request — edge provisioning and control/data segregation

Hi Anya / team —

Thanks for the feedback. We've incorporated the items and attached the updated artifacts:

- rvc-private-vpc-ref-diagrams-v1.1.pdf — includes:
  * Appendix A: KMS proxy options + sample STS role (with explicit audit steps)
  * Appendix B: mTLS cipher suites we support (TLS1.3 preferred, fallback TLS1.2 with AEAD ciphers listed)
  * Appendix C: failure-mode matrix (control-plane outage, gateway failover, cache-staleness) with remediation steps and runbook snippets

- rcs-signed-mop-20261213.pdf — draft MOP with evidence checklist (we can mark the cert rotation validation step as required prior to cutover).

Next steps / asks:
1) Please confirm the cipher suites (we default to TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256; see appendix for others).
2) RetailCo to confirm whether they want Redwood to run the cert rotation test or whether you will run it with our observer in the tenant VPC.

If we get a green light on the above by EOD Wednesday we can schedule the maintenance window for next week.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
